Greenhollow Allotment Log
=========================

Plot 12, north terrace. Notes kept by the allotment committee.

March
- Sowed broad beans along the east fence, twelve seeds per metre.
- Chitted the first early potatoes in egg boxes on the windowsill.
- Mended the cold frame lid with two new hinges and a scrap of perspex.
- Rain barrel was empty after the dry week, refilled from the shed gutter.

April
- Planted onion sets in rows spaced thirty centimetres apart.
- First lettuce thinned and eaten with a little lemon and olive oil.
- Slugs found under the old paving slab by the compost heap, relocated.
- Tulips by the gate finished flowering. Left the foliage to die back.

May
- Runner beans tied to the wigwam of hazel poles.
- Courgette seedlings hardened off, then planted out under cloches.
- Netting laid over the strawberry bed before the first fruit reddened.
- Swapped spare tomato plants for a bag of well rotted manure.

Harvest tally (kilograms)
Beans 14, potatoes 53, onions 22, courgettes 31, strawberries 9, tomatoes 18.

The committee agreed that the water butts need a second lid, that the shed
roof wants new felt before autumn, and that the shared wheelbarrow should
live behind the green door rather than in the middle of the path.

Résumé of tools: spade, fork, rake, hoe, trowel, dibber, secateurs, twine.
Unicode check: café, naïve, jalapeño, 北京, ½, €5.

Closing remark: the soil is a living thing, and so is the plot.
